US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.

llm_output.why_top_candidate_wins: signal_chile_flu has the highest composite score (7) and multiple, independent supporting links in the provided subgraph: it is a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR the failed target signal (signal_us_hosp) and it has both an IMPORTATION_LINK and a POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF relationship to the mechanism eq_us_flu_base. Those three edges directly connect the candidate to both the observed misfit (missed_peak / actual_above_prediction for hospitalizations) and to the mechanism itself, providing a clear pathway by which underestimated importation or upstream activity in Chile could cause the model to underpredict the US peak. The other candidates have weaker support: Australia has only LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR plus POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF (score 5) and Travel Importation Pressure lacks a direct leading-indicator link to the target (score 4). Therefore, Chile’s combination of a direct leading signal to the target plus two mechanism-level links makes it the most plausible single hidden driver given the available graph evidence and ranking.
llm_output.proposed_minimal_edit: Add an explicit importation forcing term from signal_chile_flu into eq_us_flu_base (e.g., link: signal_chile_flu --IMPORTATION_FORCING(lag=k)--> eq_us_flu_base) so the mechanism includes a lagged importation input proportional to recent Chile influenza activity. Test model runs with and without this single term (and a small set of plausible lags) to evaluate impact on the missed peak.
llm_output.caveat: This recommendation is based solely on the provided graph edges and scores; the presence of LEADING_INDICATOR and IMPORTATION_LINK edges indicates plausible association but not proven causation. Empirical testing (fit improvement, cross-validation, and checking alternative lags/collinearity with Australia or travel pressure) is needed before accepting the edit.
